label: Flake Hunt
description: CI flake triage: confirm it is a flake, capture evidence, isolate locally, then fix it or file a well-evidenced issue (no auto-merge).
when_to_use: Use when a CI check or test fails intermittently or on an unrelated diff and the task is to triage it. Do NOT use for a test that fails deterministically because the code is wrong — that is a 'bugfix'.

guards.message: Confirm flakiness and isolate the mechanism before committing any fix — a 'fix' for an unreproduced flake is guesswork.
This workflow does NOT merge — report the fix PR or the filed issue and stop.

steps.label: Confirm it is actually a flake
steps.guidance: Establish intermittency with evidence: `gh run list` history for the check, whether the failing scenario relates to the diff that triggered it, and a targeted re-run (`gh run rerun <id> --failed`). If it fails consistently on a clean re-run, it is not a flake — stop and switch to 'bugfix'. Done when pass/fail history is recorded and flakiness is confirmed or ruled out.

steps.label: Capture the failure evidence
steps.guidance: Pull the failing job's logs (`gh run view <id> --log-failed`) before they age out: exact test/scenario name, failure message, timing, shard/runner, and anything anomalous (timeouts, ports, ordering). Compare against a passing run of the same test. Done when the evidence is saved and the failure signature is written down.

steps.label: Isolate the mechanism locally
steps.guidance: Try to reproduce locally: run the specific test repeatedly (loop it), under load or reduced timeouts if timing-related. Identify the mechanism class — shared state between tests, timing/timeout margin, ordering dependence, external resource — and cite the code (file:line) that makes it possible. A flake you cannot reproduce after a serious attempt still gets its suspected mechanism written down with confidence level. Done when the mechanism (or best hypothesis) is recorded.

steps.label: Fix it or file it
steps.guidance: If the mechanism is confirmed and the fix is small: fix it at the mechanism level (never just widen a timeout without justifying the new margin), prove it by looping the test, then branch/commit/push through the full gate (never --no-verify) and open a PR. Otherwise: file a gh issue carrying ALL captured evidence, the suspected mechanism, and the reproduction attempts, so the next hunter starts warm. Done when either the PR is open or the issue is filed.

steps.label: Report the outcome (no merge)
steps.guidance: Report: flake confirmed or ruled out, mechanism, and the action taken (PR number or issue number). If a PR was opened, confirm CI is green (`gh pr checks <n>`) but do NOT merge. Done when reported and `git status` is clean or matches the opened PR.
